component: Mbox format and meaningful stream tests

quotes.text:
* Aims:
 * - Byte exact. What you write is exactly what should come back out when
 *   read.
 *   NOTE: There is one exception. Messages with an unterminated
 *   final line will have an EOL added. Without this, there's no way to
 *   ensure the proper message separation required for a well-formed mbox.
 * - Handles malformed messages - everything is just stored verbatim.
 * - Uses reversible "From " escaping, as per mboxrd. "From " lines are
 *   prefixed with '>'. If already prefixed, another '>' is added.
 *   e.g. "From Bob Smith" => ">From Bob Smith".
 *        ">>>>From here..." => ">>>>>From here..."
 * - Avoid intermediate copies of data. The only time buffering is required is
 *   where "From " parts are split across Write() calls.
 * - Handle processing lines of any length, without extra memory usage.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The current mbox output contract adds one > to From-prefixed lines, including already quoted lines, and buffers only an undecided start fragment across Write calls. A missing final end-of-line is the documented exception to byte-exact round trips. TestMsgMboxWrite writes each message in chunks of 1, 3 and 4096 bytes, calls Finish and compares the expected mbox after removing only runtime-dependent separator timestamps. Its BadMessages case deliberately writes malformed message bytes. A parser or stream change needs boundary-sized cases, not only one full-buffer write. Only the header, relevant completion implementation and these test sources were read; the tests were not run.
title: Keep mbox escaping reversible across writes and document the final-line exception
